cells.Values and default: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on. Unset: off. The script does not add `--export-only`.
cells.Effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) adds `--export-only` to every `build-model.py` call. `build-model.py` then writes the trace (the PyTorch export of the model) and stops. It does not start the ingest program and does not update the model config file. `build-model.py` then does not read `GHC`, `CABAL_INSTALL` or `CABAL_FLAGS`. `DUMP_ALL` has no effect.

hints.problem: Conflicting meanings of "trace". Text A, in `EXPORT_ONLY` and in the proposal of chunk tools-01: "the trace (the PyTorch export of the model)". Text B, in sections 1.10 and 3.3: a trace is a Perfetto recording of timing events. Both are real things. The rows `TRON_INGEST_LIBSTDCXX_PATH`, `MODEL_TRACE_STORE_PATH`, `TRACE_INPUTS` and `TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS` already say "model trace" for A. `EXPORT_ONLY` is the only row with the bare word.
hints.suggested: In `EXPORT_ONLY`, replace "`build-model.py` then writes the trace (the PyTorch export of the model) and stops." with "`build-model.py` then writes the model trace (the PyTorch export of the model) and stops."

cells.Set by: The Nix dev shell sets `ghc`. CMake sets it for child commands.
cells.Values and default: Name or full path of the GHC program (the Haskell compiler). CMake does not accept a directory. Unset: CMake searches only for `ghc-9.12` and `ghc`, plus `ghc-9.12.2` when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not defined. `build-model.py` uses `ghc`. Empty: `build-model.py` passes an empty `-w` value.
cells.Effect: The two readers differ. CMake configure tries the value as the last candidate name in its search for the compiler, after its fixed names. `build-model.py` passes the value to `cabal run` as the compiler option `-w`. CMake reads it only with `BUILD_INGEST_MODELS` on and `TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE` empty. A fixed name that CMake finds wins over the value. CMake caches the found path as `GHC_EXECUTABLE`. Without `IN_NIX_SHELL` the compiler must report version 9.12.2. `build-model.py` reads `GHC` only without `--ingest-bin` and `--export-only`.

hints.problem: The two variables are read by the same two files in the same way, and they sit in different sections. Their Set by cells also conflict: CMake sets both for its child commands, and only the `GHC` row says so. The row `CABAL_VERSION` says that `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` exports `CABAL_INSTALL`, and the Set by cell of `CABAL_INSTALL` does not name that script.
hints.suggested: Put both rows in one table: move `CABAL_INSTALL` from 5.5 to 3.4, between `CABAL_FLAGS` and `DUMP_ALL` (this follows the "lowest section number" rule proposed for rule 1). Replace its Set by cell with: "`flake.nix` in the Nix dev shell, and the CI workflows. CMake sets it for child commands. `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` sets it for its local rebuild."

hints.problem: Rule 1. "wins over" is a metaphor for priority. Other rows already say "takes priority". Original phrase: "wins over"
hints.suggested:
Replace one sentence in each cell. The rest of each cell stays as it is.
`GHC` (line 432): "A fixed name that CMake finds wins over the value." -> "A fixed name that CMake finds takes priority over the value."
`SLICE_REFRESH_RUN_URL` (line 800): "The option `--run-url` wins over the variable." -> "The option `--run-url` takes priority over the variable."
`SLICE_REFRESH_RUNNER_CLASS` (line 801): "The option `--runner-class` wins over the variable." -> "The option `--runner-class` takes priority over the variable."
`SLICE_REFRESH_SOURCE_SHA` (line 802): "The option `--source-sha` wins over the variable." -> "The option `--source-sha` takes priority over the variable."

cells.Values and default: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on. Unset: `build-all.sh` adds `--meta-device` to every `build-model.py` call.
cells.Effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) leaves out `--meta-device`. The export step then builds each model with zero-filled weights in CPU memory. With `--meta-device` the parameters stay on the PyTorch meta device (tensors with a shape and no data). Without `--meta-device` the memory use grows with the model size. A comment in `ingest/export/torch_export.py` calls that path legacy.

cells.Set by: A developer. `config/test_model_definitions.py` sets it for one test.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. The script does not check it. The ingest program creates the directory when it is missing. Unset: the directory `gen/src/tron/h/tron/plugins` of the checkout.
cells.Effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every ingest model of `config/models.yaml`) passes the path to `ingest/build-model.py` as `--plugin-dir`. `build-model.py` passes it to the ingest program as the output directory of the generated model plugin. With a non-empty `EXPORT_ONLY`, `build-model.py` stops after the export step and writes no plugin. The CMake variable `PLUGIN_DIR` in `ingest/CMakeLists.txt` is a separate variable. It is not an environment variable.

cells.Set by: The Nix dev shell and the derivation in `nix/model-traces.nix`.
cells.Values and default: Path of the directory that holds `libstdc++`. The script does not check the text. Unset: `build-model.py` does not change `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` of the export subprocess.
cells.Effect: `ingest/build-model.py` puts the directory at the front of `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for its export subprocess (the ingest step that exports the PyTorch model trace). Later subprocesses of the script do not get the change. The script reads it only when the export step runs. The option `--skip-export` skips that step. Nix sets it to the `libstdc++` directory of the Nix compiler on Linux, and to an empty string on other systems.

hints.problem: Rule 8. "derivation" is a Nix term with no definition. The rows `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` call the same thing "the Nix build". Two words for one thing. Original phrases: "The Nix derivation `tron-test-model-traces`", "the derivation in `nix/model-traces.nix`"
hints.suggested:
Replace:
`TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM` and `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE`: "The Nix derivation `tron-test-model-traces`" -> "The Nix build `tron-test-model-traces`"
`TRON_INGEST_LIBSTDCXX_PATH`, Set by: "The Nix dev shell and the derivation in `nix/model-traces.nix`." -> "The Nix dev shell and the Nix build in `nix/model-traces.nix`."
The out-of-scope row `TERM` has the same phrase.

cells.Values and default: File descriptor numbers separated by white space. Each item is parsed with `int`. An item that is not an integer raises `ValueError`. Unset: `build-model.py` passes no extra file descriptor to the export process.
cells.Effect: `build-model.py` passes the listed file descriptors to the process that exports the model trace. Each descriptor is a lease (an open file that holds a shared lock in the CI model weights cache). `prepare_tests.py` sets the variable only when it runs a command after `--`. It passes the same descriptors to that command. A process that did not inherit these descriptors cannot use the numbers. `build-model.py` does not read the variable when the option `--skip-export` is given.

hints.problem: The introduction says: "These are variables of scripts under `bin/ci`. Each has a default that the caller can replace." Two of the 12 rows do not fit. `TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS` is read by `ingest/build-model.py`, not by a script under `bin/ci`, and it has no default that a caller replaces. `CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S` is read by `bin/fuse_cleanup.py`. The row `TRON_INGEST_LIBSTDCXX_PATH` has the same reader as `TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS` and sits in 3.4. One of the two was placed by its reader and the other by its setter.
hints.suggested: Move `TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS` to 3.4, between `TRON_INGEST_LIBSTDCXX_PATH` and `WEIGHTS`. Replace the 6.5 introduction with: "These are variables of scripts under `bin/ci`, and of `bin/fuse_cleanup.py`, which a `bin/ci` script starts. No workflow sets them. Each has a default that the caller can replace. A row moves to 6.3 or 6.4 when a workflow starts to set the variable."

cells.Values and default: Path of model weights. `ingest/build-all.sh` passes the text unchanged as the `--default-weights` argument of `ingest/build-model.py`. Unset: the script passes no `--default-weights` for a model whose registry entry has no `default_weights`.
cells.Effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` passes the value as `--default-weights` to `ingest/build-model.py`, for each model whose entry in the model registry (`config/models.yaml`) has no `default_weights`. `build-model.py` does not use the argument in these runs. The generated files do not change. `build-model.py` uses `--default-weights` only when it adds a model configuration entry. It adds none with `--no-config`. `build-all.sh` passes `--no-config` for every model that has an architecture name. `config/model_definitions.py` gives every registry model such a name.

cells.Set by: A developer, by hand. `config/test_model_definitions.py` sets it in one test.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. It holds one sub-directory of model weights for each Hugging Face model ID. Unset: `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`.
cells.Effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` passes `<WEIGHTS_ROOT>/<model ID>` to `ingest/build-model.py` as the model path (`-m`). A model whose directory does not exist fails with `local weights not found`. A required model without a directory ends the script. An optional one is only reported. `ingest/build-model.py` does not read the variable. It has its own fixed path `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`. For a model path outside that path, it passes no `--tokenizer` argument to the export step.

cells.Values and default: Any non-empty text turns coverage mode on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on. Unset: coverage mode is off. `RUN_COVERAGE` and `COVERAGE_TIX_DIR` are not used.
cells.Effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) runs only the models that `RUN_COVERAGE` lists. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` to `<COVERAGE_TIX_DIR>/<model>.tix` for each model. At the end it combines the `.tix` files (Haskell coverage counts) of that directory into `build-all-combined.tix`. `COVERAGE` adds no coverage option to the `cabal` command. `make build-all-coverage` in `ingest/` sets `COVERAGE=1` and passes those options in `CABAL_FLAGS`. When no `.tix` file exists, the script prints a warning. The CMake option `COVERAGE` is a different setting.

cells.Set by: CI workflow `ingest-coverage.yml` sets `35`. Developers set it locally.
cells.Values and default: Whole number of percent, for example `35`. The recipe does not check the text. Text that is not an integer makes the recipe print `PASS`. Unset: the recipe stops with a shell error that contains `COVERAGE_BASELINE not set`.
cells.Effect: It is the lowest accepted expression coverage of the ingest Haskell code, in percent. The recipe rounds the measured coverage to the nearest 5 percent. The target fails when the rounded value is below the baseline. Both targets are in `ingest/Makefile`. `coverage-check` reads `coverage-summary.txt` (tests only). `coverage-check-combined` reads `coverage-summary-combined.txt` (tests and `build-all.sh` runs). CI sets `35` and runs `coverage-check-combined`. CI also reports the rounded coverage minus the baseline.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. A relative path starts at the working directory of the script. Unset: `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix` under the working directory.
cells.Effect: In coverage mode `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) creates the directory. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` to `<directory>/<model>.tix` for each model. At the end it combines all `.tix` files (Haskell coverage counts) of the directory into `build-all-combined.tix`. Used only when `COVERAGE` is not empty. `.tix` files of an earlier run are combined too. `make build-all-coverage` sets the default directory itself and deletes the `.tix` files there first. `make coverage-combine` reads only `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix/build-all-combined.tix`. The working directory of the script must be `ingest/`.

hints.problem: `make coverage-combine` reads only `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix/build-all-combined.tix`. => `coverage-combine` reads two inputs. It searches the Cabal coverage build directory for the test coverage file `ingest-tests.tix`, and it reads `build-all-combined.tix` at the fixed path `$(BUILD_ALL_TIX_DIR)`. The true part of the sentence is that the target never reads `COVERAGE_TIX_DIR`, so it does not see a `build-all.sh` result in another directory. As written, the sentence says the target has one input file. (ingest/Makefile:282)
hints.suggested: In coverage mode `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) creates the directory. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` to `<directory>/<model>.tix` for each model. At the end it combines all `.tix` files (Haskell coverage counts) of the directory into `build-all-combined.tix`. Used only when `COVERAGE` is not empty. `.tix` files of an earlier run are combined too. `make build-all-coverage` sets the default directory itself and deletes the `.tix` files there first. `make coverage-combine` does not read `COVERAGE_TIX_DIR`. It looks for the `build-all.sh` result only at `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix/build-all-combined.tix`. It also reads the test coverage file `ingest-tests.tix`. The working directory of the script must be `ingest/`.
